blocks.text: sprite?: { // a flat image facing the camera: billboard yaw (unset) turns the card to each viewer's camera, none locks it to the entity's rotation (a flat thing: a decal, a poster: edge-on from the side), full also pitches; uvRect picks a sheet region; frames named in events fire onAnimationEvent; castShadow: true throws the card's shadow in its picture's shape (a turning card's shadow turns with it) texture: AssetID size?: [number, number] // World-space [width, height] of the quad. OMIT for pixel sprites: the engine sizes the sprite from the asset's declared world height (its `2d` metadata), so pixel density stays uniform across the scene (64 px per world unit). Set it only to deliberately rescale; authored size always beats the metadata default. pixelsPerUnit?: number // Pixels-per-unit convenience; used only when `size` is omitted. Setting it also opts out of the metadata-driven default size. anchor?: [number, number] // Normalized [u, v] point of the art that sits at the entity's origin (0..1, v up; default [0.5, 0] = bottom-center "feet"). It places the quad relative to `feetPosition`, it is the pivot the sprite rotates around: a bullet spinning about its center wants [0.5, 0.5], a ceiling lantern swinging from its top wants [0.5, 1], a door hinged at an edge wants [0, 0], and the auto-derived collider2d hull is expressed against the same point, so art, pivot, and hitbox always share one origin. tint?: Color // multiplies the art opacity?: number // 0..1, blends in linear light: over a dark background white at 0.05 reads 21% solid, 0.25 reads 65%, 0.5 reads 86% blend?: SpriteBlendMode lit?: boolean // Scene lights shade the sprite (the engine derives a normal map from the art automatically). Default: in a 2D place that has any authored light, world sprites are lit automatically: painted plates (`backdrop-`, `strip-`, `floor-` art and parallax layers) stay unlit because their lighting is in the art, and an explicit true/false always wins. Places without lights render unlit. Alpha/cutout blends only: add/multiply/subtract sprites are themselves light/stain, so `lit` is a documented no-op there. emissive?: number // HDR glow (default 0). Feeds bloom; works lit or unlit. normalStrength?: number // Normal-map relief strength (default 1). 0 = pure distance falloff. billboard?: "none" | "yaw" | "full" upright?: boolean // The sprite never inherits the entity's rotation as in-plane spin; it keeps the base pose (axis-aligned under the camera) however the entity turns: NPC steering, physics, scripts. The lock covers both 2D modes. The collider of a body that is not dynamic stays with the picture too; rotation still drives children and a dynamic body. Characters whose facing is `?facing=` texture swaps want `upright: true`; leave unset for things that should visibly turn (cars, ships, banking projectiles). No effect in 3D places: `billboard` owns rotation inheritance there. flipX?: boolean flipY?: boolean sortingLayer?: number sortingOrder?: number ySort?: boolean alphaCutoff?: number cutout?: boolean // Alpha-tested cutout rendering: discard pixels below 50% alpha and write depth, so heavily overlapping sprites (foliage, crowds, dense beds) resolve per-pixel instead of haloing by draw order. Default on for pixel-inferred art (`pixel-*` names, `?animated=` atlases, `scripts/tex-*.js` refs), off for painterly art, which sorts whole-sprite by distance: set true on a painterly sprite that lives among others, false for soft/glow edges. filter?: "pixel" | "linear" // Texture sampling override. "pixel" samples nearest (crisp pixel art), "linear" samples smooth. Unset defers to the asset's own pixel-ness (moodboard grammar / metadata inference). parallax?: [number, number] // Scroll factors [x, y] of a background picture; the sim never moves it. 1 = fixed in the world (default), 0 = fixed to the camera, between = parallax (far hills ~0.2–0.5, near trees ~0.7). It draws at feet + (1 − factor) × camera: the first factor on x, the second on z in a 2d-top place and on y elsewhere. A `backdrop-` picture in a 2D place whose second factor is not 1 also stays on screen on that axis. repeatX?: boolean // Tile the sprite's texture along X. On camera-attached sprites the quad spans the viewport and the texture scrolls its UV phase (the strip recipe). On plain world sprites this only sets the sampler's wrap: the sprite keeps its own class (lit stays lit, batched stays batched); use `uvRect` width > 1 for the tile count, or pair with `feetPosition: { attach: "camera" }` for an endless band. uvRect?: SpriteUvRect // Normalized texture-space rectangle; UV origin is bottom-left. Inside 0..1 it crops (a still cell of a sheet). Reaching past 0..1 tiles: the sampler wraps on that axis: `{ x: 0, y: 0, width: 4, height: 1 }` repeats the art 4× across the quad, with no lighting or batching side effects. A negative width or height reads the crop mirrored (the sprite-engine mirror); zero is refused. events?: Record<string, Record<number, string>> | null // Frame events, per clip: `events: { run: { 3: 'footfall', 7: 'footfall' } }`: the clip name a mixer channel plays, the frame index (clip-local) that fires the named event exactly when the winning channel's clock shows that frame. The object's behavior receives it as `onAnimationEvent(ctx, { name, animation, frame })`: footsteps, attack hitboxes, emitter bursts that never drift from the art. Set null to remove. Costs nothing on sprites without it. trail?: { interval?: number; life?: number; count?: number; tint?: Color | [Color, Color]; fade?: "alpha" | "shrink" | "both"; blend?: "normal" | "additive" } | null // Afterimage trail, dash ghosts, motion echoes: `trail: { interval: 0.04, life: 0.3, fade: 'both' }`. The engine snapshots the sprite's pose + frame + tint every `interval` seconds and draws the snapshots behind the sprite, fading out over `life` seconds (`fade`: 'alpha' | 'shrink' | 'both'; `tint` recolors the ghosts; `count` caps them). `tint` also takes a `[head, tail]` ramp of two colours lerped per ghost by age. `blend: 'additive'` renders the ghosts add-blended for energy/glow dashes (the sprite itself keeps its own blend). Ghosts are frozen copies: they never animate. Set null to remove. Costs nothing on sprites without it. material?: ScriptedMaterialSpec // A scripted material draws the sprite's pixels: `{ kind: "scripted", script, params }`, the contract an object's material takes; what it reads of the sprite is ctx.sprite (spawn api builtin/three). The sprite keeps its size, frames, flips, tint, opacity, blend, cutout and sorting; the material's class decides its light, so lit, emissive and normalStrength do nothing. Each distinct params value is its own batch and its own draw. A broken script draws the plain sprite until the next edit. } // "sprite" is also in: builtin/three (SpriteNodeMaterial)
